## Overview

**GitHub Desktop** is a standalone application (separate from RStudio)
that lets you do most everyday Git operations through a graphical
interface instead of the command line. This is a quick reference for
the buttons and panes you'll see there.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The Changes List

| Column / Icon | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Checkbox | Whether the file is **staged** — included in the next commit. Select **Select All** at the top of the list (or check the box next to "Changes") to select all files |
| Icon next to file name | A yellow dot = modified, a green plus = added (new/untracked), a red minus = deleted |

> All files must be **staged** (checkbox ticked) before they can be
> committed. By default, GitHub Desktop stages all changed files
> automatically when you open it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Diff / Review Changes

- Click a file's name (not the checkbox) in the left-hand list to open
  the **diff viewer** on the right
- Red lines = removed, green lines = added
- This is your chance to review exactly what will be committed —
  always worth checking before committing

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Commit

1.  Tick the checkboxes for the files you want to include
2.  Type a short, informative **summary** in the box at the
    bottom-left (e.g., `Fix data cleaning bug`)
3.  Optionally add a longer **description** below the summary box
4.  Click **Commit to \<branch-name\>**

A commit is a saved snapshot of your staged changes, stored locally.
It is **not** sent to GitHub until you **push**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Push

- Click **Push origin** in the top toolbar to send your local commits
  to GitHub
- The button shows a number (e.g., "Push origin 1") indicating how
  many commits are waiting to be pushed
- You should see the commits you pushed on the GitHub website as soon
  as you refresh the page
- Do this regularly, so all versions are up to date

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Pull (Fetch origin)

- Click **Fetch origin** in the top toolbar to check for new commits
  on GitHub
- If there are new commits, the button changes to **Pull origin** —
  click it to merge them into your local branch
- Do this regularly, and especially before starting new work, to avoid
  falling behind or creating conflicts

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## History

- Click the **History** tab (next to the **Changes** tab, top-left)
- Shows every commit on the current branch: summary, author, date, and
  hash
- Click any commit to see the diff introduced by that commit
- Useful for figuring out *when* a change was made or *what* changed

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Ignore

- Right-click a file in the **Changes** list → **Ignore file** (or
  **Ignore file extension...**)
- Adds the file/pattern to `.gitignore`, so Git never tracks or
  uploads it to GitHub (e.g., `*.Rproj.user`, `.Rhistory`, large data
  files, private data or notes)
- Ignored files disappear from the Changes list and are not pushed to
  GitHub but remain on your hard drive

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Discard Changes (Revert)

- Right-click a file in the **Changes** list → **Discard changes...**
- Discards **uncommitted** changes to that file, restoring it to the
  last committed version
- ⚠️ This is destructive — uncommitted edits are lost permanently
  (GitHub Desktop moves them to the Recycle Bin/Trash as a small
  safety net)

> To undo something already **committed and pushed**, don't use
> Discard Changes. Look up how to revert to a previous commit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Branches

The current branch name is shown in the **Current branch** dropdown in
the top toolbar.

### Create a new branch

1.  Click **Current branch** → **New branch**
2.  Name it (e.g., `add-analysis`)
3.  Click **Create branch**
4.  Click **Publish branch** to also create it on GitHub

You are automatically switched onto the new branch.

### Switch between branches

1.  Click **Current branch**
2.  Select the branch you want from the list
3.  GitHub Desktop switches your working files to match that branch

> Commit or stash changes before switching branches — GitHub Desktop
> will warn you if switching would overwrite uncommitted work.

### Merge a branch

- The **Branch** menu → **Merge into current branch...** lets you
  merge one local branch into another
- More commonly, push your branch, then open a **pull request on
  GitHub.com** and merge it there (see
  `Exercise_GitHub_Branching.Rmd`)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick Reference Table

| Action | Where in GitHub Desktop |
|----|----|
| See what changed | Click file name → diff viewer |
| Stage a file | Tick its checkbox |
| Save a snapshot | Summary box → **Commit to \<branch\>** |
| Send commits to GitHub | **Push origin** |
| Get others' commits | **Fetch origin** → **Pull origin** |
| View past commits | **History** tab |
| Stop tracking a file | Right-click → **Ignore file** |
| Discard uncommitted changes | Right-click → **Discard changes...** |
| Create a branch | **Current branch** → **New branch** |
| Switch branches | **Current branch** → select branch |
| Merge a branch | **Branch** menu, or a pull request on GitHub.com |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Conclusion

GitHub Desktop covers the everyday workflow — stage, commit, push,
pull — plus branch creation and switching, all outside of RStudio. For
anything it doesn't do directly (resolving complex conflicts, undoing
pushed commits), GitHub.com's web interface or the Git command line
are the next steps.
